description: Beyond Gravity is a passionate team of technology enthusiasts aiming to leverage satellite data, data science, and software development to address real-world environmental challenges through innovative solutions.
summary: FireAtlas is an interactive web application that harmonizes NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspots from MODIS and VIIRS into a single, comparable burning activity calendar for any selected area of interest. Satellites have tracked fire for more than two decades, but the record is split across sensors that cannot be compared directly, leaving fire managers without a consistent picture of when and where burning occurs. FireAtlas closes that gap with daily and monthly calendars, a 3D globe, year-over-year comparison, fire radiative power analysis, and preliminary anomaly insights that flag unusual conditions and critical fire periods. Consider a researcher monitoring fire activity in Assam for a single month: MODIS records 120 detections and VIIRS records 185. Rather than treating these as 305 separate fires, FireAtlas brings both into a sensor-aware view so the researcher can compare detection patterns and FRP without equating detections with unique fire incidents. Unobserved periods appear as unknown coverage, not zero activity, and every view exports as a report. FireAtlas supports researchers, forest departments, disaster management agencies, educators, and policymakers in early warning, monitoring, and evidence-based decisions
details:
FireAtlas is an interactive platform that transforms NASA FIRMS satellite observations from MODIS and VIIRS into an accessible view of global fire activity.
Because these satellites differ in observation frequency, resolution, and data availability, comparing their records can be challenging. FireAtlas brings both datasets into one platform for geographic exploration, temporal analysis, and sensor comparison.

🔬 How It Works

FireAtlas follows a structured data-processing and visualization workflow:

  1. Satellite Data Acquisition: Uses NASA FIRMS active-fire observation datasets from MODIS and VIIRS.
  2. Data Processing: Organizes observations using geographic coordinates, acquisition dates, sensor information, and relevant fire parameters.
  3. Geographic Exploration: Allows users to investigate global observations or select specific regions using bounding-box geographic boundaries.
  4. Sensor-Aware Analysis: Compares MODIS and VIIRS observations while accounting for differences in sensor characteristics and data availability.
  5. Temporal Analysis: Summarizes observed fire activity across daily and monthly periods to reveal changing patterns.
  6. Interactive Visualization: Presents the results through a 3D globe, charts, fire activity calendars, and Fire Radiative Power (FRP) visualizations.
  7. Reporting: Provides structured analytical information and downloadable reports for further exploration and documentation.
💡 Key Innovation: Coverage-Aware Fire Analysis

FireAtlas accounts for differences in satellite data availability to prevent misleading fire activity comparisons.

For example, if MODIS and VIIRS records are available from January to July, but only MODIS data is available in August, FireAtlas marks missing VIIRS observations as unknown, not zero.

It also distinguishes satellite detections from unique fires, burned area, and confirmed damage.

Our focus: Making satellite fire analysis more transparent, comparable, and scientifically responsible.

🚀 Key Benefits and Intended Impact

FireAtlas turns complex satellite observations into accessible insights for:

  • Researchers: Analyze fire trends and compare satellite data.
  • Forest Departments: Monitor regional fire activity.
  • Universities: Explore and understand Earth observation data.
  • Disaster Agencies: Support preliminary fire assessments.
  • Environmental Organizations: Communicate findings through visual reports.

Impact: Making satellite fire data easier to explore, interpret, and use for environmental monitoring.

💻 Tools and Technologies

FireAtlas is being developed using a modular web application architecture.

  • NASA FIRMS: Primary source of active-fire satellite observations.
  • MODIS and VIIRS: Satellite instruments providing complementary fire observations.
  • Python 3.11: Backend development and data-processing workflows.
  • FastAPI: Backend API development and data-service architecture.
  • Pydantic: Request validation and structured data models.
  • Uvicorn: Backend application server.
  • CSV and structured datasets: Regional observation storage and processing.
  • Interactive Web Technologies: For the 3D globe, geospatial visualization, charts, calendars, and dashboard interface.
🎨 Creativity and Design Approach

Our creative approach focuses on making complex satellite data easy to explore and understand. FireAtlas brings geographic visualization, temporal analysis, sensor comparisons, and observation coverage into one interactive platform.

We prioritized scientific accuracy, data transparency, usability, and flexible geographic exploration through global and bounding-box selection.

Our vision is to bridge the gap between raw satellite observations and meaningful environmental understanding — helping people see not just where satellites detect fires, but understand what the observations actually reveal.
